title.en: What led 34 Australians to the remote Nepal valley hit by deadly floods?
title.zh: 是什么导致 34 名澳大利亚人来到遭受致命洪水袭击的偏远尼泊尔山谷？

summary.en: Dozens of Australians are missing in Nepal's Langtang Valley, a popular destination.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
At least 34 Australians are missing after a flood and landslide disaster on the Nepal-Tibet border, with many caught up in one of Nepal's most popular trekking regions, the remote Langtang Valley.

Some 403 tourists — 341 of them foreigners — were unaccounted for several hours after the disaster struck on Wednesday , according to Nepal's tourism ministry. Chinese rescuers are searching for hundreds more in Tibet.

It's feared many more are missing or dead, as rescuers battle a lack of infrastructure and remote, mountainous terrain to search through mud and debris.

Foreign Minister Penny Wong spoke about why so many foreign nationals were in the area in a press conference on Thursday afternoon.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

"It is well–known that this area, people are not only going there for trekking but also for spiritual reasons, so you would anticipate that the foreign nationals who were in the region would have been there for a variety of reasons," Wong said.

She said it may take time for the Australian government and Nepalese authorities to understand how many people are missing or dead.

"I can only outline the numbers we are aware of today," Wong said. "The numbers of foreign nationals are higher and as yet we do not have any further information about if there are any more of those who are Australian.

"We will continue to try to ascertain if there are any Australians who are not accounted for over and above the 34 that we are aware of."

United States-based tourist company Himalayan Glacier confirmed 15 Australians who were on one of its tours are missing and unaccounted for in the Langtang Valley.

The company's chief executive said he had not been able to contact the group of 47 people — which includes 15 Australians, nine Nepalese, two from the United Kingdom, two from Singapore and others from the US and Russia, the ABC has reported.

Among the Australians missing are nine men and six women. The youngest are boys aged 14 and 11, and the oldest is a woman aged 64.

The flood hit Syabrubesi, is the starting point for the popular Langtang trek, as well as other areas used by travellers for Hindu pilgrimage to Kailash Mansarovar.

It's not the standard Mount Everest trekking route, but the valley it leads to — Langtang Valley — is the third most popular trekking area in Nepal, just behind Everest and the Annapurna region.

Langtang is a narrow valley running north from the Syabrubesi gateway, hemmed in by snow-capped peaks — including mountain Langtang Lirung, which stands over 7,000m tall — with icy landscapes, rivers and glaciers lining the route.

title.en: 'Creative thinking is born of loneliness': Artist Yayoi Kusama dies at 97
title.zh: “创造性思维源于孤独”：艺术家草间弥生去世，享年 97 岁

summary.en: Japan's "polka dot queen" has been remembered for her remarkable originality.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The dotty pumpkins and kaleidoscope rooms of Yayoi Kusama, who has died aged 97, were as vibrant as the artist herself, but her exuberant work was the expression of a long battle with mental illness.

Once a fixture of the 1960s pop and minimalist scenes in New York, Japan's "polka dot queen" found huge commercial success in her later decades.

Her larger-than-life paintings, sculptures and installations — inspired by vivid hallucinations — sold for millions of dollars and packed out top galleries.

Kusama, instantly recognisable in her bright red wig and bold spotted outfits, worked well into old age from the psychiatric hospital in Tokyo where she lived voluntarily for the second half of her life.

But she also struggled with her feelings for her home country, which she left for decades and once described as "full of disdain for women".

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Born in 1929, the youngest daughter of a wealthy but troubled family, Kusama started producing her signature dot and net patterns at the age of 10.

"My mother had regrets about my birth, and I was driven to the edge psychologically," she wrote in her autobiography, A Personal History of Polka Dots.

"One day, after seeing a tablecloth with a red flower pattern on a desk, I saw the same red flower pattern all over the ceiling, windows and pillars. It filled the room, and covered my body."

Art provided a release for the young Kusama, whose father, a seedling merchant, was unfaithful to her mother.

"When I was sad or lonely, everything would be cured when I drew pictures," she said.

In the book, Kusama explained her concept of "self-obliteration" — a recurrent theme throughout her career.

"I put dots all over my body and make all the surroundings dot patterns. By creating the same thing over and over, my own existence is buried in the art."

Kusama studied Japanese painting in Kyoto, against her parents' wishes, and held her first solo exhibition in 1952 in her hometown of Matsumoto in central Japan.

At the show, she met a psychiatrist who advised her to go and work abroad — an idea that appealed to her.

"Japan was so small, vulgar, feudalistic and full of disdain for women," said the artist.

"I was born and raised in Japan, but I'm not influenced by Japanese culture and tradition."

The decisive push to pack her bags came when she wrote to modernist painter Georgia O'Keeffe, who encouraged Kusama to seek international recognition in the United States.

Kusama moved to Seattle in 1957 and then to New York, where she struggled to find her place as an Asian artist in the city's largely white, male-dominated creative scene.

title.en: At least one dead after car crashes into crowd in northern France
title.zh: 法国北部汽车冲撞人群 至少一人死亡

summary.en: One suspect was arrested after the incident in Caen, police said, following a reported fight at a nearby bar.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
At least one person has been killed and 10 people injured after a car crashed into a group of people near a train station in northern France, police say.

A male suspect was later arrested after authorities launched a major emergency response in Caen, in the Normandy region.

Local prefect David Claviere said seven of those injured were in a critical condition and three more had minor injuries, AFP reported.

The incident took place near a bar, with local media reporting that a fight had broken out there before the incident took place.

"For the moment, we are not dealing with a terrorist motive, but the investigation is only just beginning," said Bruno Coutanceau, a top security official for Caen.

All of the victims appeared to be men between the ages of 17 and 40, he told AFP.

Claviere said that the car "deliberately drove into pedestrians in the street opposite the train station".

The suspect, a 26-year-old man born in Russia, was later arrested around 20km (12 miles) away in the port town of Ouistreham.

He was not previously known to intelligence services and police had been aware of him "only for traffic offences", Claviere said.

Social media videos from the scene appeared to show crowds gathering around police cars and ambulances, where a large area was cordoned off.

A spokesperson for the local administration of Calvados told the BBC that some of those injured were receiving treatment in the emergency ward of a nearby hospital.

Police have opened an investigation into the incident, which will be led by detectives from Caen's Specialised Crime Division.

body.zh: 警方称，法国北部火车站附近一辆汽车撞向一群人，造成至少 1 人死亡、10 人受伤。 当局在诺曼底地区卡昂启动重大紧急响应后，一名男性嫌疑人随后被捕。 据法新社报道，当地州长戴维·克拉维埃尔 (David Claviere) 表示，其中 7 名伤者情况危急，另有 3 人受轻伤。 事件发生在一家酒吧附近，当地媒体报道称，事发前酒吧曾发生过斗殴事件。 卡昂高级安全官员布鲁诺·库坦索表示：“目前，我们处理的不是恐怖主义动机，但调查才刚刚开始。” 他告诉法新社，所有受害者似乎都是 17 岁至 40 岁之间的男性。 克拉维埃说，这辆车“故意冲撞火车站对面街道上的行人”。 嫌疑人是一名出生于俄罗斯的 26 岁男子，后来在约 20 公里（12 英里）外的港口城市乌伊斯特勒昂被捕。 克拉维埃说，情报部门此前并不了解他，警方“只是因为交通违法行为”才认识他。 现场的社交媒体视频似乎显示，人群聚集在警车和救护车周围，大片区域被封锁。 卡尔瓦多斯当地政府发言人告诉英国广播公司，其中一些伤者正在附近一家医院的急诊室接受治疗。 警方已对这起事件展开调查，调查将由卡昂特别犯罪部门的侦探领导。 获取我们的旗舰新闻通讯，其中包含您开始新的一天所需的所有头条新闻。在这里注册。

title.en: At least 12 dead as wildfires sweep through northern Algeria
title.zh: 阿尔及利亚北部山火造成至少12人死亡

summary.en: Northern Africa has experienced severe heatwaves this summer, leading to hundreds of fires across the region.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
At least 12 people have been killed and dozens injured as wildfires burn through large swathes of northern Algeria.

Civil protection authorities said dozens of blazes swept through several provinces along the country's northern coastline.

At least 54 people had suffered burn injuries, with at least six of them being treated in intensive care, Interior Minister Said Sayoud said on Wednesday night.

The deaths comes as northern Africa swelters under a severe heatwave, with Tunisia and Algeria particularly affected.

Sayoud said five people were killed in Jijel province, four in Bejaia and three in Tizi Ouzou.

He has travelled to Bejaia with the Algerian Health Minister Mohamed Seddik Ait Messaoudene to "assess" local firefighting and evacuation efforts, government officials said.

Many homes in Bejaia and Jijel have been evacuated, according to the civil protection agency and local media.

Footage shared by local broadcaster Jijel News showed residents taking refuge in a post office as thick clouds of smoke billowed around them.

Firefighters were battling 69 blazes across the country, the civil protection agency said earlier on Wednesday evening.

The Bejaia region saw devastating fires tear through forest and farmland three years ago when 30 people were killed.

Last month, authorities recorded at least six deaths caused by fires, with crews battling more than 2,000 blazes across Algeria in July alone.

While Algeria regularly experiences forest fires around the summer months, climate change has exacerbated the intensity and severity of recent wildfires in the country.

The World Meteorological Organization (WMO) said extreme heat had become common in North Africa, a region that has seen the most rapid warming of the six subregions of Africa – 0.43C per decade - between 1991 and 2025.

Rising heat and water shortages have also led to an increase in camel deaths during summer heatwaves in Algeria, a recent study revealed.
body.zh: 阿尔及利亚北部大片地区发生野火，已造成至少 12 人死亡、数十人受伤。 民防部门表示，数十场大火席卷了该国北部海岸线的几个省份。 内政部长赛义德·萨尤德周三晚表示，至少 54 人烧伤，其中至少 6 人正在重症监护室接受治疗。 这些死亡事件发生之际，北非正在经历严重的热浪，其中突尼斯和阿尔及利亚受到的影响尤其严重。 萨尤德说，吉杰勒省有 5 人死亡，贝贾亚有 4 人死亡，提济乌祖有 3 人死亡。 政府官员表示，他与阿尔及利亚卫生部长穆罕默德·塞迪克·艾特·梅萨乌德内一起前往贝贾亚，“评估”当地的消防和疏散工作。 据民防机构和当地媒体报道，贝贾亚和吉杰勒的许多房屋已被疏散。 当地广播公司 Jijel News 分享的视频显示，居民们在一家邮局避难，周围浓烟滚滚。 民防机构周三晚间早些时候表示，消防队员正在全国范围内扑灭 69 起火灾。 三年前，贝贾亚地区的森林和农田发生了毁灭性火灾，造成 30 人死亡。 上个月，当局记录了至少 6 人因火灾死亡，仅 7 月份，救援人员就在​​阿尔及利亚各地扑灭了 2,000 多起火灾。 虽然阿尔及利亚在夏季经常发生森林火灾，但气候变化加剧了该国最近发生的野火的强度和严重程度。 世界气象组织（WMO）表示，北非的极端高温现象已经很普遍，该地区是非洲六个次区域中升温最快的地区，1991年至2025年间每十年升温0.43摄氏度。 最近的一项研究显示，气温上升和水资源短缺也导致阿尔及利亚夏季热浪期间骆驼死亡人数增加。

title.en: 'If you started running, they shot you' - inside Nigeria's growing kidnapping crisis
title.zh: “如果你开始逃跑，他们就会开枪射杀你”——尼日利亚日益严重的绑架危机

summary.en: Many communities are living in fear of being kidnapped for ransom as the crisis spreads further south.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
"If you ran into a room, they set the room on fire," says Fatima, describing a recent attack on her village in Zamfara, north-western Nigeria. "If you came out and started running, they shot you."

The gunmen, who struck at 02:00, split into groups to surround residents: one at the village entrance, one in the centre and one at the back.

"They opened fire without a care in the world, shooting indiscriminately," the 55-year-old quietly tells the BBC World Service.

It was one of many attacks that have caused havoc in the mainly Muslim community where residents live in fear of being kidnapped for ransom.

Fatima explains how the raids unfold: "You could have 100 motorcycles, and each one could be carrying three people."

About 70 people, including children, were killed from the village of Bia Buki in June, according to Fatima.

She describes how the attackers also targeted villagers as they fled and children were injured falling into ditches. Among the dead were her husband and six of his seven siblings.

Fatima is one of an estimated 800,000 Nigerians who the UN says have been displaced in the country's north-west. One of the main reasons people have left their homes is violence.

Some attacks have been carried out by militant Islamist groups, but the majority in this region are by gangs, locally referred to as bandits, who often move around on motorcycles and attack quickly then ride away, escaping before security forces arrive.

Thousands of people have joined government-backed vigilante groups to fight, and the BBC spoke to one who said his armed group had killed many bandits.

But the gangs keep attacking in what appears to be a deteriorating pattern of violence and abductions that is spreading southwards.

Fatima says when the bandits attacked her home, she ran into the nearby forest with other villagers to hide: "The forest became our sanctuary. We ran with our kids, if you couldn't find your child you'd take your neighbour's child."

She says people slept in the forest before moving on to the state capital, Gusau, "where we found a little bit of peace".

Fatima now lives in an informal camp in Gusau with her seven children, who are aged between nine and 30.

Dozens of women sit in groups on the dusty ground of the makeshift compound, many wearing brightly coloured hijabs. More than 1,000 people are here, she believes.

Conditions are tough with "no proper place to even lay your head". Food is scarce and assistance arrives irregularly.

Fatima describes two occasions where "good Samaritans" brought rice or potatoes. Children are sent out to gather firewood to sell so families can buy food, but 22 have been kidnapped by bandits, she says.

Gesturing towards a nearby building, Fatima says that there "you will find 100 or more women… maybe just...
body.zh: “如果你跑进一个房间，他们就会放火烧毁房间，”法蒂玛在描述尼日利亚西北部扎姆法拉村庄最近发生的袭击事件时说道。 “如果你出来并开始逃跑，他们就会开枪打死你。” 枪手于凌晨 02:00 发动袭击，他们分成几组包围居民：一组在村口，一组在中间，一组在后面。 “他们毫不关心地开枪，不分青红皂白地开枪，”这位 55 岁的老人平静地告诉 BBC 国际频道。 这是在以穆斯林为主的社区造成严重破坏的众多袭击事件之一，那里的居民担心被绑架勒索赎金。 法蒂玛 (Fatima) 解释了突袭行动的过程：“你可以拥有 100 辆摩托车，每辆摩托车可载三人。” 据法蒂玛称，6 月份 Bia Buki 村约有 70 人被杀，其中包括儿童。 她描述了袭击者如何在村民逃跑时瞄准村民，以及儿童掉入沟渠受伤的情况。死者包括她的丈夫和他七个兄弟姐妹中的六人。 联合国表示，估计有 80 万尼日利亚人在该国西北部流离失所，法蒂玛就是其中之一。人们离开家园的主要原因之一是暴力。 一些袭击是由激进的伊斯兰组织发动的，但该地区的大多数袭击是由当地被称为土匪的帮派所为，他们经常骑着摩托车四处移动，迅速发动袭击，然后骑车离开，在安全部队到达之前逃跑。 数千人加入了政府支持的自卫队参加战斗，英国广播公司采访了一位表示他的武装组织杀死了许多土匪的人。 但这些团伙仍在继续发动袭击，暴力和绑架事件似乎正在不断恶化，并正在向南方蔓延。 法蒂玛说，当强盗袭击她的家时，她和其他村民一起跑进附近的森林躲藏起来：“森林成了我们的避难所。我们带着我们的孩子跑，如果你找不到你的孩子，你就会带走邻居的孩子。” 她说，人们在前往州首府古绍之前先在森林里睡觉，“在那里我们找到了一点平静”。 法蒂玛现在和她的七个孩子住在古绍的一个非正式营地，他们的年龄在 9 岁到 30 岁之间。 数十名妇女成群结队地坐在临时院落尘土飞扬的地面上，其中许多人戴着色彩鲜艳的头巾。她相信这里有超过 1,000 人。 条件艰苦，“连睡觉的地方都没有”。食物匮乏，援助的到来也不稳定。 法蒂玛描述了两次“好心的撒玛利亚人”带来大米或土豆的情况。她说，孩子们被派去收集柴火出售，以便家人购买食物，但有 22 名孩子被土匪绑架。 法蒂玛指着附近的一栋建筑说，“你会发现 100 名或更多的女性……也许只是……”

title.en: Iceland holds knife-edge referendum on EU - and it could be decided on fish
title.zh: 冰岛就欧盟问题举行全民公投 - 可能会以鱼类决定

summary.en: On Saturday, Iceland will vote on EU membership talks, amid economic and geopolitical tensions.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Inside a waterfront factory, workers in hairnets and blue overalls are sorting freshly caught cod and haddock, and machines process the fish into fillets, mostly bound for Europe.

Visir fishing boss Pétur Pálsson, who fears joining the European Union would cost Iceland jobs and drive factories abroad, says: "If we are in the EU, they will be the ones who make the policy."

On Saturday, voters in this island nation of almost 400,000 people will decide whether their country should resume talks on joining the EU. It is a referendum that polls suggest is too close to call.

Supporters think closer European ties could help tame Iceland's volatile currency and soaring cost of living.

Opponents say Iceland's sovereignty and control over "priceless" fishing waters are at stake, and would rather continue going it alone.

It is a fault line that has divided Icelanders for decades, but after winning a snap election in 2024 Prime Minister Kristrún Frostadóttir's centre-left government pledged to hold a referendum by 2027.

Russia's war in Ukraine, sharpening Arctic rivalries and US President Donald Trump's tariff threats and designs on Greenland have accelerated that timetable.

"Things have been moving very rapidly with respect to geopolitical challenges," Finance Minister Daði Már Kristófersson tells the BBC, pushing Iceland's place in the world "up the agenda".

Iceland lies high in the North Atlantic, adjacent to a strategic stretch of sea called the GIUK gap, where Russian maritime activity is closely watched by the West.

One poll this week put the Yes vote ahead by 51.3% to 48.7%; an earlier poll had the two camps neck and neck.

"It's impossibly [hard] to predict," says Eirikur Bergmann, professor of politics at Bifröst University. "Both camps are throwing everything they have at it."

Kristoffersen's Liberal Reform party is a leading voice behind the Yes campaign.

He argues that EU membership would strengthen Iceland's security and trade position, and shield it from much bigger powers.

There's the economic case too. "We see the opportunity of joining the EU and adopting the euro as a very significant benefit to Icelandic companies and to the Icelandic general public," he says.

A Yes vote would kickstart negotiations with Brussels, but a second referendum would have to greenlight any final membership deal. The EU's 27 members would have to agree to it too.

Some Icelanders are expected to vote Yes as this is not the final referendum anyway. "We have to know what's in the package from the EU," says Reykjavik resident Anna Ragnarsdottir. "If we say no, we won't ever know."

Although outside the EU, Iceland is part of the European Economic Area (EEA) along with Norway and Liechtenstein, so it is part of the single market and the Schengen border-free...
body.zh: 在一家海滨工厂内，戴着发网、穿着蓝色工作服的工人正在对新鲜捕获的鳕鱼和黑线鳕进行分类，机器将鱼加工成鱼片，大部分运往欧洲。 维西尔渔业老板 Pétur Pálsson 担心加入欧盟会导致冰岛失业，并将工厂迁往国外，他说：“如果我们在欧盟，政策的制定者将是他们。” 周六，这个拥有近 40 万人口的岛国的选民将决定他们的国家是否应该恢复加入欧盟的谈判。民意调查显示，这是一场势均力敌的公投。 支持者认为，更紧密的欧洲关系可能有助于抑制冰岛汇率波动和生活成本飙升。 反对者表示，冰岛的主权和对“无价”捕鱼水域的控制受到威胁，他们宁愿继续单打独斗。 这条断层线几十年来一直分裂着冰岛人，但在 2024 年提前选举中获胜后，总理克里斯特伦·弗罗斯塔多蒂尔 (Kristrún Frostadóttir) 领导的中左翼政府承诺在 2027 年之前举行全民公投。 俄罗斯在乌克兰的战争、加剧的北极竞争以及美国总统唐纳德·特朗普对格陵兰岛的关税威胁和设计加速了这一时间表。 财政部长达迪·马尔·克里斯托弗松 (Daði Már Kristófersson) 告诉 BBC，“地缘政治挑战方面的情况进展非常迅速”，这将冰岛在世界上的地位推上了“议程”。 冰岛位于北大西洋高处，毗邻被称为GIUK缺口的战略海域，西方国家密切关注俄罗斯的海上活动。 本周的一项民意调查显示，赞成票以 51.3% 对 48.7% 领先；早些时候的民意调查显示，两个阵营旗鼓相当。 “这很难预测，”比弗罗斯特大学政治学教授埃里库尔·伯格曼 (Eirikur Bergmann) 说。 “两个阵营都在竭尽全力。” 克里斯托弗森领导的自由改革党是“是”运动背后的主要声音。 他认为，加入欧盟将加强冰岛的安全和贸易地位，并使其免受更大势力的侵害。 还有经济情况。 “我们认为加入欧盟和采用欧元的机会对冰岛公司和冰岛公众来说是一个非常重大的好处，”他说。 如果投票赞成，将启动与布鲁塞尔的谈判，但第二次公投必须批准任何最终的成员资格协议。欧盟 27 个成员国也必须同意。 预计一些冰岛人会投赞成票，因为无论如何这都不是最终的公投。雷克雅未克居民安娜·拉格纳斯多蒂尔 (Anna Ragnarsdottir) 表示：“我们必须知道欧盟的一揽子计划中有哪些内容。” “如果我们说不，我们就永远不会知道。” 尽管在欧盟之外，冰岛与挪威和列支敦士登一样是欧洲经济区（EEA）的一部分，因此它是单一市场和申根无边界的一部分......

title.en: A landmark US deal could change social media forever
title.zh: 美国达成里程碑式协议，或将永远改变社交媒体

summary.en: Meta Platforms has agreed to pay up to $25 billion over the next decade to settle lawsuits from nearly all 50 US states alleging that Facebook and Instagram were designed to addict children. The deal includes strict new limits on how teenagers interact with these platforms to address concerns over mental health and...
summary.zh: Meta公司已同意在未来十年内支付高达250亿美元，以解决美国近50个州发起的诉讼。这些州指控Facebook和Instagram的设计旨在让儿童成瘾。该协议还包括对青少年使用这些平台的严格新限制，以应对对其心理健康和安全的担忧。

body.en:
Meta Platforms will pay up to US$18 billion ($25 billion) over the next decade and strictly limit how teenagers use Facebook and Instagram under an agreement with nearly all 50 US states that took it to trial to resolve claims it designed those social media platforms to addict children.

The settlements announced on Wednesday end a federal trial over allegations Meta's products harmed children, and the company misled the public about their safety. Four of the states — California, Colorado, Kentucky and New Jersey — were expected to seek close to US$200 billion ($279 billion) in civil penalties.

While Meta will not undergo a fundamental overhaul, the accords represent a sweeping effort to define how it serves young users.

It could provide a template for resolving thousands of other lawsuits against social media companies. Governments around the world are trying to curb children's access to harmful online content, including a ban in Australia on social media for children under 16.

“The focus of this case was to protect our kids," Colorado Attorney General Phil Weiser said in a statement. "The relief we are getting in this settlement is very meaningful and well beyond what any court has ordered or is likely to order."

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Meta agreed over the next decade to restrict teenagers' use of Facebook and Instagram to two hours a day and block all usage from midnight to 6am, absent parental consent.

These limits could be tightened if the social media platforms Snapchat, TikTok and YouTube adopt similar terms. Meta will also disable most push notifications to teenage users during school hours of 8am to 3pm and enhance measures to prevent children from accessing age-restricted content.

The settlement does not require Meta to abandon personalised recommendations or targeted advertising. It also does not address some content Meta researchers found particularly problematic, including posts that made Instagram users uncomfortable with their body image.

Meta denied wrongdoing in agreeing to settle. The total payout represents about three to four months of profit and about one month of revenue for Meta.

"Ensuring teens have a safe and productive experience on our platforms is an absolute imperative for Meta," the Menlo Park, California-based company said in a blog post. "We want to get this right for parents and teens."

Meta agreed to make maximum payments of about US$16.7 billion ($22 billion) to 47 U.S. states, Washington, D.C., Puerto Rico, American Samoa and the Northern Mariana Islands.

title.en: Australian tour group among 1,300 missing people in Nepal-Tibet floods
title.zh: 尼泊尔洪水和山体滑坡造成数百人失踪，其中包括澳大利亚人

summary.en: Aid workers have described scenes of complete destruction, with entire settlements "wiped out".
summary.zh: 救援人员描述了彻底毁灭的景象，整个定居点“被夷为平地”。

body.en:
Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has confirmed 34 Australians are missing after a massive flood and landslide disaster on the Nepal-Tibet border killed at least 165 people on Wednesday, with hundreds more unaccounted for.

Another 823 people, including 579 Nepali and foreign tourists, remained out of contact in Nepal, according to the country's disaster agency.

Across the border, Chinese state media said the "mudslide disaster" at the Gyirong Port in Tibet claimed three lives while 558 people, including 260 foreigners, were still missing.

"At this point, there are 34 Australians who are missing," Albanese told a press conference on Thursday morning. "People would have seen some of the footage, which is a truly horrific event."

Albanese said it was difficult to obtain information from Nepali authorities and appealed to anyone with information to come forward.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

"At this point, Nepal is a developing country. It doesn't have the resources that an event like that would have in Australia, so information is difficult.

"Our thoughts are with all those who will be concerned about their loved ones today."

Defence minister Penny Wong echoed the Prime Minister's statements, noting that the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT) was working "urgently" to ascertain the welfare and location of the missing Australians.

"We are currently deploying further DFAT personnel, including crisis response experts to the region to ensure that we do provide the support needed to these posts, particularly our post in Nepal," Wong in a press conference on Thursday.

"At this stage, access and information are very limited given the scale of disaster. We will do our best, to ascertain whatever information we can."

A US-based tour company Himalayan Glacier Adventures told ABC News that 15 Australians, part of a group of 47 people, were on a hiking tour in the Lantang Valley at the time of the landslides.

The group of Australians was comprised of nine men and six women. Two of those Australians were reportedly boys aged 11 and 14, and a woman aged 64.

Tilak Pokharel, president of the Australian Nepalese Multicultural Centre, said there were "a lot" of people in Melbourne waiting anxiously to hear from loved ones.

"There are a lot of people affected by the flood. There are many people from that area living in Melbourne," Pokharel said.

"But several of them lost their property. I was just talking to someone who is from that area and they lost their houses, they lost their property and they have nothing left at the moment.

"I was talking to someone who was saying people went to see the flooding and they lost their life."

reflection.en: The news of hundreds missing and entire settlements "wiped out" by floods and landslides in Nepal brings immense sorrow. In moments of such widespread devastation and loss of life, the brevity of "Jesus wept" reminds us that grief is a natural and holy response. Yahweh, in Christ, shares in our human pain, offering a compassionate presence when words fail.
reflection.zh: 尼泊尔洪水和山体滑坡造成数百人失踪、整个定居点“被夷为平地”的消息，带来了巨大的悲痛。在如此大规模的毁灭和生命损失面前，“雅伟哭了”这简短的经文提醒我们，悲伤是一种自然而神圣的回应。雅伟在基督里分担我们人类的痛苦，当言语无法表达时，祂提供了一个充满怜悯的同在。

title.en: Rocky Horror Picture Show star Tim Curry dead at 80
title.zh: 《洛奇恐怖秀》主演蒂姆·克里去世，享年80岁

summary.en: Tim Curry, the English actor famous for his role as Dr. Frank-N-Furter in The Rocky Horror Picture Show, has died at 80 after struggling with his health for over a decade following a 2012 stroke.
summary.zh: 英国演员蒂姆·克里因在邪典音乐电影《洛奇恐怖秀》中饰演弗兰克-N-弗特博士而闻名，他在2012年中风后与病魔抗争十余载，现已去世，享年80岁。

body.en:
Tim Curry, the English actor best known for his star turn as Dr Frank-N-Furter in the cult classic musical film The Rocky Horror Picture Show, has died at the age of 80, US media reported on Thursday.

Curry, who had struggled with his health for more than a decade after a debilitating stroke, died at his home in Los Angeles, TMZ said, citing unnamed sources.

The actor, who launched his career in London's West End theatre district, first played the gender-bending mad scientist in Rocky Horror before reprising the role in the 1975 film, still a staple of midnight cinema showings more than 50 years later.

His other credits include the sinister clown Pennywise in a 1990 television miniseries version of Stephen King's It and films that included Charlie's Angels and Muppet Treasure Island.

An impressive theatrical resume that began in the 1960s saw him do turns at the Royal Court Theatre and the Citizens Theatre, taking on roles written by Shakespeare, Brecht and Tom Stoppard, among others.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Curry was nominated for Tony and Olivier awards for his theatre work in New York and London.

One of his more memorable performances was on Broadway and in the West End as King Arthur in Monty Python's Spamalot, the stage adaptation of Monty Python and the Holy Grail.

His slightly cartoonish good looks and an unparalleled ability to both camp and vamp meant he was in high demand for roles that required a certain air of villainy.

That was on display in Annie in 1982, when, as con artist Rooster Hannigan, he plots to kidnap the orphan girl.

Three years later, in Clue, he was the butler who corralled a country house full of murder suspects in the cinematic version of the board game.

There were straighter roles, including opposite Sean Connery in The Hunt for Red October, but his comedic talents shone brightest, even in small parts, like the Plaza Hotel concierge in Home Alone 2.

But it was Dr Frank-N-Furter, the "sweet transvestite from Transsexual, Transylvania", that defined his career.

Richard O'Brien's madcap stage creation tells the story of an unsuspecting young couple whose flat tyre leads them into the house of a scientist who is creating a cross-dressing sexual plaything.

Along the way, there's a lot of singing, dancing and a heavy dose of rocker Meatloaf.

The film, which flopped on its initial release, found life as a cult classic on the midnight showings circuit, with aficionados dressing up to sing and dance in the aisles and throw popcorn — and frankfurters — at the screen.

"It seemed like something that would go," Curry told a TV interviewer in 1970s London.

"I was hesitant in that, if it...
body.zh: 据美国媒体周四报道，英国演员蒂姆·库里 (Tim Curry) 去世，享年 80 岁。 TMZ 援引未透露姓名的消息人士称，库里在中风后十多年来一直与健康作斗争，最终在洛杉矶的家中去世。 这位演员在伦敦西区剧院区开始了自己的职业生涯，他首先在《洛基恐怖片》中扮演了性别扭曲的疯狂科学家，然后在 1975 年的电影中再次扮演这个角色，该片在 50 多年后仍然是午夜电影院的主要放映内容。 他的其他作品包括 1990 年斯蒂芬·金电视迷你剧《It》中的险恶小丑 Pennywise，以及《查理的天使》和《布偶金银岛》等电影。 从 20 世纪 60 年代开始，他的戏剧履历令人印象深刻，他在皇家宫廷剧院和公民剧院轮流演出，扮演莎士比亚、布莱希特和汤姆·斯托帕德等人创作的角色。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 库里因其在纽约和伦敦的戏剧作品而获得托尼奖和奥利弗奖提名。 他最令人难忘的表演之一是在百老汇和伦敦西区的《巨蟒剧团与圣杯》舞台剧《火腿骑士》中饰演亚瑟王。 他略显卡通化的英俊外表以及无与伦比的露营和吸血能力意味着他很适合需要某种邪恶气氛的角色。 1982 年的《安妮》就展现了这一点，当时他作为骗子鲁斯特·汉尼根 (Rooster Hannigan) 密谋绑架孤女。 三年后，在《线索》的电影版棋盘游戏中，他扮演管家，将一栋乡间别墅里挤满了谋杀嫌疑人。 他也有一些比较直率的角色，包括在《猎杀红色十月》中与肖恩·康纳利演对手戏，但他的喜剧天赋最耀眼，即使是在小角色中，比如《小鬼当家 2》中的广场酒店礼宾部。 但真正定义了他职业生涯的是“来自特兰西瓦尼亚变性人的可爱异装癖”弗兰克-N-富特博士。 理查德·奥布莱恩的疯狂舞台创作讲述了一对毫无戒心的年轻夫妇的故事，他们的轮胎漏气了，他们走进了一位正在创造异装性玩具的科学家的房子。 一路上，有很多歌声、舞蹈和大量的摇滚乐 Meatloaf。 这部电影在首次上映时遭遇失败，后来在午夜放映中成为了一部邪典经典，影迷们盛装打扮，在过道里载歌载舞，并向银幕投掷爆米花和法兰克福香肠。 “这似乎是一件会发生的事情，”库里在 20 世纪 70 年代的伦敦接受电视采访时说道。 “我当时很犹豫，如果...

reflection.en: The news of Tim Curry's passing at 80, after a decade-long struggle with his health following a stroke in 2012, reminds us of the body's fragility. Yet, even as our physical selves may waste away, the Scripture offers hope that our inner spirit can be renewed day by day. This perspective encourages us to find strength and purpose beyond outward...
reflection.zh: 蒂姆·克里在2012年中风后与病魔抗争十余载，最终于80岁离世的消息，提醒我们身体的脆弱。然而，即使我们的外在身体日渐衰败，圣经仍赐予我们盼望，我们的内在精神可以日日更新。这种视角鼓励我们在外在环境之外寻找力量和目的，信靠雅伟在生命每个季节中持续的恩典。

verse.textEn: Therefore we do not lose heart. Though outwardly we are wasting away, yet inwardly we are being renewed day by day.
verse.textZh: 所以，我们不丧胆。外体虽然毁坏，内心却一天新似一天。

title.en: Meta settles in US states lawsuit on teen user addiction
title.zh: Meta 在美国各州针对青少年用户成瘾的诉讼中达成和解

summary.en: Meta has agreed to pay what could amount to billions of dollars and to implement platform usage limitations on young users in a lawsuit brought by US states. The challenge revolved around addiction issues and overuse.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.zh: 在美国各州提起的诉讼中，Meta 同意支付可能高达数十亿美元的费用，并对年轻用户实施平台使用限制。挑战围绕成瘾问题和过度使用。 Facebook 和 Instagram 的母公司 Meta 同意支付高达 167 亿美元（约合 143 亿欧元），并对青少年使用其社交媒体网站的方式施加新的限制，作为美国多个州在加利福尼亚州提起诉讼的一部分。 该提案于周三向联邦法院提交，旨在解决美国总共 47 个州联盟提出的索赔要求。 除了经济损失之外，预计 Meta 还会引入各种限制和变更，旨在改善儿童安全，阻止或防止夜间或上课期间的过度使用和社交媒体活动。 加州总检察长罗布·邦塔 (Rob Bonta) 在宣布和解协议时在一份声明中表示：“Meta 已同意进行大规模变革，以降低其平台造成损害的风险，并将在几个月内完成。” 他称该协议是“真正的改变、真正的透明度以及对儿童的真正可执行的保护”。 该文件指出，该协议并不意味着 Meta 承认责任或不当行为，Meta 一直否认这些指控。 然而，弗吉尼亚州总检察长杰伊·琼斯认为，梅塔故意将年轻人的健康置于危险之中，而这些变化有助于阻止这种情况。 琼斯说：“多年来，Meta 故意欺骗公众，让公众了解其令人上瘾和有害的设计功能，这些功能对青少年的心理健康造成了严重破坏。”他认为，和解协议“将结束这些危险的做法，并提供有意义的救济，保护儿童免受网络伤害。” Meta 提出了针对 18 岁以下人群的一系列使用限制，其中包括对每天在其网站上花费的总时间设置“硬性上限”。 Meta 各个平台的全天累积上限设置为每日使用 2 小时。家长将有权解除限制。 Meta 表示，如果它检测到拥有多个帐户的不同用户，它将适用于所有用户。 午夜至早上 6 点期间，未成年用户也将被暂停使用该网站。 在 Meta 所称的“学校模式”中，通知将在上午 8 点到下午 3 点之间默认静音，青少年在这些时间段内不再收到推送通知，“除了有关其帐户安全的直接消息和警报”。 在美国大多数州，在 Facebook 和 Instagram 上开设帐户的最低年龄为 13 岁（在某些情况下甚至更高），因此理论上对于年幼的孩子来说应该没有问题。加州总检察长表示...

title.en: Could Syria become the focus of an Israeli-Turkish conflict?
title.zh: 叙利亚会成为以色列与土耳其冲突的焦点吗？

summary.en: An Israeli attack on a Syrian military airfield just recently demonstrated once again that Syria is becoming a key battleground for the rivalry between regional powers. At the forefront: Israel and Turkey.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
An Israeli attack on a Syrian military airfield just recently demonstrated once again that Syria is becoming a key battleground for the rivalry between regional powers. At the forefront: Israel and Turkey.

Following US mediation, Syrian and Israeli representatives met in Jordan last weekend for the first time in months. The talks aimed to defuse tensions following the recent Israeli attacks on Syrian territory and prevent hostilities between Israel and Turkey from spilling over into Syria.

The escalation was sparked by an Israeli attack on the Abu Duhur military airfield in Syria's Idlib Province on August 18. According to Syrian sources, the attack struck the runway and storage facilities without causing any fatalities. Israel stated that Syria had violated — or threatened to violate — a previous security agreement by allowing Turkish troops to use the airfield. The governments of both Syria and Turkey rejected these allegations.

 The United States criticized the attack by its Israeli ally as an "unnecessary escalation." In diplomatic terms, this amounts to a fairly clear show of rhetorical support for Ankara  and Damascus .

Israel views a potential Turkish military presence in Syria as a red line . Yet, it remains unclear whether such a deployment is planned in the long term or whether it was even imminent at the time of the attack. Evidence on this matter is not publicly available.

However, as early as April 2025, Reuters news agency cited anonymous sources saying Turkey had inspected at least three air bases in Syria  where it might want to station troops  as part of a planned joint defense pact. Israeli airstrikes were already taking place at that time as well.

The Washington-based think tank Foundation for Defense of Democracies (FDD), which is considered pro-Israel, justifies the attack as follows : "Israel worries that Ankara could eventually use its military presence in Syria as a platform to pressure or threaten Israel, and remains wary of the close relationship between Syrian President Ahmad al-Sharaa and the Turkish leadership."

For Bente Scheller, Syria expert at the German Green Party-affiliated Heinrich Böll Foundation, this explanation falls short.

"There is no evidence so far that Turkish troops are actually supposed to be stationed there," she told DW.  While Israel may indeed have its own intelligence, the recent attack must be viewed against the backdrop of Israel's overall policy toward Syria as well as Turkey's growing regional role, she noted.

Marcus Schneider, a Middle East analyst at Germany's Friedrich Ebert Foundation — which is affiliated with the German Social Democratic Party (SPD) — in Beirut, also points out that a struggle for power and influence is unfolding in Syria and...
body.zh: 不久前以色列对叙利亚军用机场的袭击再次表明，叙利亚正在成为地区大国博弈的关键战场。走在前列的是以色列和土耳其。 在美国的调解下，叙利亚和以色列代表上周末在约旦举行了数月来的首次会面。会谈旨在缓和以色列最近袭击叙利亚领土后的紧张局势，并防止以色列和土耳其之间的敌对行动蔓延到叙利亚。 事态升级是由以色列8月18日袭击叙利亚伊德利卜省阿布杜胡尔军用机场引发的。据叙利亚消息人士称，这次袭击袭击了跑道和储存设施，没有造成任何人员死亡。以色列表示，叙利亚允许土耳其军队使用该机场，违反了或威胁违反了之前的安全协议。叙利亚和土耳其政府均否认了这些指控。 美国批评其盟友以色列的袭击是“不必要的升级”。从外交角度来说，这相当于对安卡拉和大马士革相当明确的口头支持。 以色列将土耳其在叙利亚的潜在军事存在视为红线。然而，目前尚不清楚这种部署是否是长期计划，或者在袭击发生时是否迫在眉睫。有关此事的证据尚未公开。 然而，早在 2025 年 4 月，路透社就援引匿名消息人士的话说，土耳其已经检查了叙利亚的至少三个空军基地，作为计划中的联合防御协议的一部分，土耳其可能希望在那里驻军。以色列当时也已经开始空袭。 总部位于华盛顿的智库捍卫民主基金会（FDD）被认为是亲以色列的，它为这次袭击辩护如下：“以色列担心安卡拉最终可能利用其在叙利亚的军事存在作为向以色列施压或威胁的平台，并对叙利亚总统艾哈迈德·沙拉和土耳其领导人之间的密切关系保持警惕。” 对于德国绿党下属的海因里希伯尔基金会的叙利亚专家本特·谢勒来说，这种解释是不够的。 她告诉德国之声：“到目前为止，没有证据表明土耳其军队实际上应该驻扎在那里。” 她指出，虽然以色列可能确实拥有自己的情报，但必须在以色列对叙利亚的总体政策以及土耳其日益增强的地区作用的背景下看待最近的袭击。 德国弗里德里希·艾伯特基金会（隶属于德国社会民主党（SPD））驻贝鲁特的中东分析师马库斯·施奈德也指出，叙利亚和……正在展开争夺权力和影响力的斗争。

title.en: Zambia after the polls: A test for democracy in Africa
title.zh: 赞比亚大选后：对非洲民主的考验

summary.en: Zambia's democratic institutions are under scrutiny, as the opposition continues to dispute the election results and courts remain closed. Weeks after the election, Zambia’s election story might be far from over.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及领导、智慧与公共责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Zambia's democratic institutions are under scrutiny, as the opposition continues to dispute the election results and courts remain closed. Weeks after the election, Zambia’s election story might be far from over.

The Electoral Commission of Zambia has declared incumbent President Hakainde Hichilema winner of the August 13 presidential election .

His closest challenger, Brian Mundubile, received 38% of the vote, according to official results published last week. However, Mundubile has since announced on several occasions that he would be challenging that result , and that his National Reconciliation Party for Unity and Prosperity (NRPUP) "shall not relent" in the face of any obstacle.

That challenge, however, comes as Zambia's courts have all remained closed since August 24 until further notice, with officials citing "security concerns."

The timing of this closure has raised questions about opposition voices having access to judicial election safeguards during this crucial stage of the post-election process, as random reports of irregularities continue to surface.

The Law Association of Zambia (LAZ) has called for the urgent restoration of access to the courts and for alternative arrangements to be enacted for urgent cases.

LAZ President Arnold Kaluba said security measures must not undermine any access to justice or judicial independence.

"Such measures must be lawful, proportionate and implemented in a manner that preserves access to justice and respects the constitutional independence and autonomy of the judiciary," he stressed.

Meanwhile, the Human Rights Commission of Zambia has also expressed concern; its chairperson, Pamela Towela Sambo, warned that disruption to judicial operations could affect fundamental rights in the country, including access to a fair trial and legal remedies.

"[If] the right to a fair trial is delayed, there is increased risk of arbitrary detentions, while access to remedies is effectively blocked," she said.

However, the ongoing election dispute has taken a new turn: Zambia's Chief Justice Mumba Malila, acknowledged on August 25 that he had received documents described as a presidential election petition through his private email-address.

Malila described the method of submission as "highly irregular" —despite the current circumstances allowing no access to legal procedures. He said he nevertheless referred the documents to the Constitutional Court to determine whether this qualified as a petition having been formally filed.

The distinction here is important: The receipt of such documents does not confirm that a presidential election petition has been formally lodged per se.

The latest development comes as the courts remain...
body.zh: 赞比亚的民主机构正受到审查，反对派继续对选举结果提出异议，法院仍然关闭。选举几周后，赞比亚的选举故事可能还远未结束。 赞比亚选举委员会宣布现任总统哈凯恩德·希奇莱马 (Hakainde Hichilema) 在 8 月 13 日的总统选举中获胜。 根据上周公布的官方结果，他最接近的挑战者布莱恩·蒙杜比莱 (Brian Mundubile) 获得了 38% 的选票。然而，蒙杜比莱此后多次宣布他将挑战这一结果，并且他的民族团结与繁荣和解党（NRPUP）面对任何障碍“都不会松懈”。 然而，这一挑战正值赞比亚所有法院自 8 月 24 日以来一直关闭，直至另行通知，官员们以“安全问题”为由。 随着关于违规行为的随机报告不断浮出水面，关闭的时间引发了人们对反对派声音在选举后进程的这一关键阶段能否获得司法选举保障的质疑。 赞比亚法律协会 (LAZ) 呼吁紧急恢复诉诸法庭的机会，并针对紧急案件制定替代安排。 LAZ 主席阿诺德·卡鲁巴 (Arnold Kaluba) 表示，安全措施不得损害任何诉诸司法的机会或司法独立。 他强调说：“此类措施必须合法、相称，并以维护诉诸司法的机会并尊重宪法规定的司法独立和自治的方式实施。” 与此同时，赞比亚人权委员会也表达了担忧；其主席帕梅拉·托维拉·桑博 (Pamela Towela Sambo) 警告称，司法运作中断可能会影响该国的基本权利，包括获得公平审判和法律补救的机会。 “[如果]公平审判的权利被推迟，任意拘留的风险就会增加，而获得补救的机会实际上就会受到阻碍，”她说。 然而，正在进行的选举争议出现了新的转折：赞比亚首席大法官蒙巴·马利拉 (Mumba Malila) 于 8 月 25 日承认，他通过其私人电子邮件地址收到了所谓总统选举请愿书的文件。 马里拉将提交方式描述为“高度不规则”——尽管目前情况不允许诉诸法律程序。他说，尽管如此，他还是将这些文件提交给宪法法院，以确定这是否符合正式提交请愿书的资格。 这里的区别很重要：收到此类文件并不确认总统选举请愿书本身已正式提交。 最新进展是在法院仍然...

title.en: India: Assam tea industry faces climate-driven labor crisis
title.zh: 印度：阿萨姆邦茶叶产业面临气候驱动的劳工危机

summary.en: Plantations in Assam produce more than half of India's tea. But rising heat is hurting yields, workers are increasingly leaving for more stable work, and producers are feeling the squeeze of stagnant tea prices.
summary.zh: 阿萨姆邦的种植园生产了印度一半以上的茶叶。但气温升高正在损害产量，工人越来越多地离开去寻找更稳定的工作，而生产商则感受到茶叶价格停滞不前的压力。

body.en:
Plantations in Assam produce more than half of India's tea. But rising heat is hurting yields, workers are increasingly leaving for more stable work, and producers are feeling the squeeze of stagnant tea prices.

The problems facing upper Assam's tea gardens are becoming increasingly difficult to ignore for workers like Bidesh Kamar and Sumitra Tanti.

Recent floods disrupted work for weeks in the northeast Indian state , adding even more uncertainty to their already precarious livelihood. More than 50 tea gardens were damaged following a devastating storm that swept across parts of Assam.

"Life has become unpredictable," Tanti told DW. "The weather can disrupt work, while wages remain low and work is not as dependable as it once was," she added.

"Tea is not as profitable as it once was, and there is less certainty about the work," Kamar told DW.

After 15 years working on tea plantations, Kamar is now considering whether it is time to "move on to greener pastures."

Their experience points to a growing problem for Assam's tea industry. With the business becoming less profitable and working conditions more uncertain, the industry is struggling to retain the experienced workforce which forms the backbone of the state's tea production.

Assam produces about 52% of India's tea and supports around 700,000 plantation workers and 140,000 small tea growers.

For generations, its tea plantations have depended on a vast workforce picking leaves by hand.

But that model is now under pressure as the climate gets hotter , tea becomes less profitable and locals increasingly look elsewhere for work.

Oversupply has pushed prices down, while higher wages, fertilizer and fuel costs are squeezing producers.

Sanjiv Gogoi, who owns the 400-acre (162-hectare) Sanjiv Tea estate, said tea producers are grappling with a whole range of problems.

"Productivity has fallen, and the labor supply is not always reliable. More workers are leaving the plantations because the work no longer pays enough," Gogoi told DW.

The pressure is even greater on small growers, who produce nearly half of Assam's tea, he said.

"They have little bargaining power and often have to sell their freshly picked leaves to factories at low prices."

At the same time, erratic rainfall , rising temperatures and new pests are reducing yields and making traditional tea-growing areas increasingly vulnerable.

In Assam's major tea-growing districts, temperatures now regularly reach 36 to 40 degrees Celsius (97-104 degrees Fahrenheit), putting both tea plants and workers under severe heat stress .

Research shows that every 1°C rise in temperature can reduce tea yields by about 87 kilos per hectare in India.

body.zh: 印度一半以上的茶叶产自阿萨姆邦的种植园。但气温上升正在损害产量，越来越多的工人离开去寻找更稳定的工作，生产商也感受到了茶叶价格停滞的压力。 对于像比德什·卡马尔（Bidesh Kamar）和苏米特拉·坦蒂（Sumitra Tanti）这样的工人来说，阿萨姆邦上游茶园面临的问题变得越来越难以忽视。 最近的洪水使印度东北部邦的工作中断了数周，给他们本已岌岌可危的生计增添了更多的不确定性。一场席卷阿萨姆邦部分地区的毁灭性风暴导致 50 多个茶园遭到破坏。 “生活变得不可预测，”坦蒂告诉德国之声。 “天气可能会扰乱工作，而工资仍然很低，工作也不像以前那么可靠，”她补充道。 卡马尔告诉德国之声：“茶叶不再像以前那样有利可图，而且工作的确定性也降低了。” 在茶园工作了 15 年之后，卡马尔现在正在考虑是否是时候“转向更绿色的牧场”了。 他们的经验表明阿萨姆邦茶业面临着一个日益严重的问题。随着业务利润下降和工作条件更加不确定，该行业正在努力留住经验丰富的劳动力，而这些劳动力构成了该州茶叶生产的支柱。 阿萨姆邦生产印度约 52% 的茶叶，养活着约 70 万名种植园工人和 14 万名小型茶农。 几代人以来，茶园一直依赖大量劳动力手工采摘茶叶。 但随着气候变暖、茶叶利润下降以及当地人越来越多地到其他地方寻找工作，这种模式现在面临压力。 供应过剩导致价格下跌，而工资、化肥和燃料成本的上涨则给生产商带来压力。 Sanjiv Gogoi 拥有占地 400 英亩（162 公顷）的 Sanjiv 茶园，他表示茶叶生产商正在努力解决一系列问题。 “生产力下降，劳动力供应并不总是可靠。越来越多的工人离开种植园，因为工作报酬不再足够，”戈戈伊告诉德国之声。 他说，小种植者面临的压力更大，他们生产阿萨姆邦近一半的茶叶。 “他们几乎没有议价能力，常常不得不以低价将刚采摘的叶子卖给工厂。” 与此同时，不稳定的降雨量、不断上升的气温和新出现的害虫正在降低产量，使传统茶产区变得越来越脆弱。 在阿萨姆邦的主要茶产区，气温现在经常达到 36 至 40 摄氏度（97-104 华氏度），使茶树和工人都承受着严重的热应激。 研究表明，气温每升高 1°C，印度每公顷茶叶产量就会减少约 87 公斤。 对于花几个小时在户外采摘茶叶的茶叶工人来说，...

reflection.en: The struggles of tea plantation workers in Assam, like Sumitra Tanti, whose lives have become "unpredictable" due to rising heat, floods, and stagnant wages, echo the ancient cries of harvesters. Yahweh hears the plight of those whose labor is undervalued and whose livelihoods are made precarious by changing conditions and economic pressures. This story...
reflection.zh: 阿萨姆邦茶园工人的挣扎，例如苏米特拉·坦蒂（Sumitra Tanti），她们的生活因气温升高、洪水和工资停滞而变得“不可预测”，这与古代收割者的呼声相呼应。雅伟听见那些劳动力被低估、生计因气候变化和经济压力而变得岌岌可危的人的困境。这个故事提醒我们倾听弱势群体的声音，并为所有辛勤劳动者争取公平的条件。

verse.textEn: Look! The wages you failed to pay the workers who mowed your fields are crying out against you. The cries of the harvesters have reached the ears of Yahweh Almighty.
verse.textZh: 工人给你们收割庄稼，你们亏欠他们的工钱，这工钱有声音呼叫，并且那收割之人的冤声已经入了万军之主的耳了。

title.en: Nepal flash flood live updates: more than 1,000 people missing after glacial collapse at Tibet border
title.zh: 尼泊尔山洪突发更新：冰川崩塌致藏边界百余人失踪

summary.en: At least 165 people have died following a flash flood caused by a glacial collapse near the Nepal-Tibet border. Hundreds of foreign nationals from various countries are among the missing. Eyewitnesses on the Tibetan side described trees and electricity poles being knocked down by the rapidly advancing floodwaters.
summary.zh: 由于冰川崩塌引发的山洪暴发，已造成至少165人死亡。来自多个国家的数百名外国公民失踪。在边境的藏族一侧，目击者描述了洪水冲倒树木和电线杆的场景。

body.en: At least 165 people have died, while officials say hundreds of foreign nationals from India, the US, UK, Australia, Malaysia and Ukraine among those missing. Follow the latest news Flash floods on Nepal-Tibet border leave scores dead and hundreds missing Tell us: have you been affected by the flash floods? Eyewitness accounts have been emerging from the Tibetan side of the border , with a woman saying she was travelling from Gyirong town towards Nepal on Wednesday morning when her group encountered the flood about 4km from Gyirong port. “Trees and electricity poles had already been knocked down, and the flood water was bearing down on us. We didn’t dare turn around, so we could only reverse,” the woman, surnamed Fang, told Xiaoxiang Morning News . I was really scared. My whole body was trembling. Continue reading...
body.zh: 至少有 165 人死亡，官员称失踪者中有数百名来自印度、美国、英国、澳大利亚、马来西亚和乌克兰的外国人。关注最新消息 尼藏边境山洪造成数十人死亡、数百人失踪 告诉我们：您受到山洪影响了吗？来自边境西藏一侧的目击者称，一名妇女称，周三早上她从吉隆镇前往尼泊尔，当时她的团队在距离吉隆口岸约 4 公里处遭遇了洪水。 “树木、电线杆都被冲倒了，洪水向我们扑来，我们不敢掉头，只能倒车。”方女士告诉潇湘晨报。我真的很害怕。我的整个身体都在颤抖。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The devastating flash flood in Nepal, triggered by a glacial collapse, serves as a stark reminder of the immense power of natural forces and the fragility of human life. The earth itself, in its current state, groans under the weight of sin and decay, a reality that touches us all through such tragic events. In these moments of overwhelming loss, we are...
reflection.zh: 尼泊尔因冰川崩塌引发的毁灭性山洪，是对自然力量的巨大威力以及人类生命脆弱性的严峻提醒。大地本身在其现状下，因罪恶和败坏而呻吟，这一现实通过如此悲惨的事件触及我们所有人。在这些压倒性的损失时刻，我们被呼召与哀痛者一同哀哭，并持守未来复兴的盼望。

verse.textEn: We know that the whole creation has been groaning as in the pains of childbirth right up to the present time.
verse.textZh: 我们知道，一切受造之物一同叹息、劳苦，直到如今。

title.en: Nepal-Tibet flash floods: Death toll rises, more than 1,300 missing after glacial collapse
title.zh: 尼泊尔-西藏山洪：冰川崩塌后死亡人数上升，逾1300人失踪

summary.en: Rescue teams are searching for survivors after a glacial collapse triggered catastrophic floods in Nepal and Tibet. Hundreds of foreign tourists are missing.
summary.zh: 救援队正在搜寻幸存者，此前一场冰川崩塌引发了尼泊尔和西藏的灾难性洪水。数百名外国游客失踪。

body.zh: 尼泊尔和西藏冰川崩塌引发灾难性洪水后，救援队正在寻找幸存者。数百名外国游客失踪。 尼泊尔和西藏边境的特大山洪造成的死亡人数已上升至至少 165 人，近 1,400 人失踪。 周四，救援队正在寻找幸存者，一天前，冰川崩塌导致一面巨大的泥石墙席卷喜马拉雅社区，席卷了整个村庄。 尼泊尔国家减灾和管理局表示，该国共有 826 人失踪，其中近 600 人是外国人。 在西藏，中国中央电视台报道吉隆县有 558 人失踪，其中包括 260 名外国人。截至周四上午，该地区已确认三人死亡，两名村民获救。 灾难于周三发生，冰川崩塌引发博特科希河支流伦德科拉河洪水泛滥，该河是连接加德满都和拉萨的徒步旅行者和朝圣者常去的走廊。 尼泊尔警方发言人阿比·纳拉扬·卡夫勒(Abi Narayan Kafle)告诉路透社，死亡人数预计将继续攀升：“死亡人数将会上升，因为我们已经恢复搜索，预计将找到更多尸体。” 旅游局发言人苏尼尔·夏尔马 (Sunil Sharma) 告诉美联社，失踪者中有 133 名是前往西藏冈仁波齐峰的印度朝圣者，该山是印度教徒的圣地，另外还有 47 名美国人、34 名澳大利亚人、33 名英国人和 24 名加拿大人。 路透社援引警方和旅游官员的数据略有不同，称失踪游客有 177 名印度游客、63 名美国游客、34 名澳大利亚游客、33 名英国游客和 25 名加拿大游客。 如果您信赖我们团队的可信报道，请花点时间选择我们作为您在 Google 上的首选来源，这样您始终会首先看到我们经过验证的新闻。

reflection.en: The earth itself groans, awaiting redemption. This catastrophic flood, born from a melting glacier, is a stark reminder of the fragility of our world and the deep impact of sin on creation. As we mourn the lives lost and search for the missing, we can also pray for the healing of the earth and the ultimate renewal promised in God's kingdom.
reflection.zh: 大地万物一同叹息，等待着被救赎。这场由冰川融化引发的灾难性洪水，鲜明地提醒我们世界的脆弱以及罪对受造界的深远影响。在哀悼逝者、搜寻失踪者的同时，我们也能祈求大地得到医治，并盼望神国度中那终极的更新。

verse.textEn: We know that the whole creation has been groaning as in the pains of childbirth right up to the present time.
verse.textZh: 我们知道，一切受造之物一同叹息、劳苦，直到如今。

title.en: What caused the catastrophic flash flood in Nepal and Tibet – and how does a glacier collapse?
title.zh: 尼泊尔和西藏的灾难性山洪暴发原因何在——冰川如何崩塌？

summary.en: Flash floods that swept through the Nepal-Tibet border region on Wednesday have left scores dead and more than 1000 people missing. An avalanche from a glacier is believed to be the likely cause, with climate change also being investigated.
summary.zh: 周三席卷尼泊尔-西藏边境地区的山洪已造成数十人死亡，1000多人失踪。据信，冰川崩塌引发的雪崩是造成山洪的可能原因，气候变化也正在调查中。

body.en:
Did a massive glacial collapse in the Himalayas trigger the disaster and is climate change involved?

Flash floods that swept through the Nepal-Tibet border region on Wednesday have left scores dead and more than 1000 people missing. Here’s what we know so far, and what likely caused the disaster.

An avalanche from a glacier is believed to be the likely cause of the flash flooding.

Local media reported Nepal’s foreign minister, Shisir Khanal, told the country’s parliament on Wednesday that initial reports suggested the floods could have been caused by an earthquake in the ⁠area that triggered a landslide.

However, the US Geological Survey (USGS) said that while the event was initially reported to be caused by a magnitude 4.4 earthquake, further analysis showed the “seismic event was a glacial collapse and debris flow that caused subsequent catastrophic impacts downstream” and “no earthquake had occurred”.

The USGS noted the glacial collapse had registered as a magnitude 5.2 seismic event on the Richter scale, occurring near the border between Nepal and China at 8.37am local time on Wednesday.

According to Assoc Prof Daniel Shugar, a geomorphologist at the University of Calgary in Canada, initial satellite analysis showed a 0.2 sq km chunk of ice “collapsed about 1.2km vertically”.

“What I can see in … satellite imagery from Planet Labs, the lower part of a glacier broke off at about 5,200 metres and crashed onto the valley floor about 1,200 metres below,” he ​said.

That was “likely enough to have converted a lot of potential to kinetic (heat) energy, melting the ice”, he wrote on Bluesky .

The satellite imagery also seemed to show that a large ‌amount of snow had melted in the 24 hours prior to the disaster, he said. “Some of the glaciers in the valley were covered in snow yesterday and today they are mostly bare ice. So in other words (and I haven’t seen any weather station data yet), it was probably warm.”

Prof Andrew Mackintosh, a glaciologist at Monash University in Melbourne, said it was unclear whether the collapse was isolated to the glacier, or was the “whole mountainside collapsing that included part of the glacier”.

“When a glacier of that scale collapses, it generates a lot of water, and then there’s a cascading sequence of events … where the water and the sediment combine and bulks up and creates the flood.”

An international group of glacier researchers has said that while a glacial collapse was “certainly involved”, it was “unlikely to be the sole cause”.

“These sorts of large glacier collapses are really shocking,” Mackintosh said. “It’s hard as a glaciologist not be alarmed by these events that seem different to what we’ve observed previously.”

However, he said “there have been so few of these documented that we’re not...
body.zh: 喜马拉雅山大规模冰川崩塌是否引发了这场灾难？是否与气候变化有关？ 周三席卷尼泊尔和西藏边境地区的山洪已造成数十人死亡、1000多人失踪。以下是我们目前所知的情况，以及可能导致这场灾难的原因。 据信，冰川雪崩可能是山洪爆发的原因。 当地媒体报道称，尼泊尔外交部长希西尔·卡纳尔 (Shisir Khanal) 周三向该国议会表示，初步报告显示，洪水可能是由该地区发生的地震引发的山体滑坡造成的。 不过，美国地质调查局(USGS)表示，虽然最初报道该事件是由4.4级地震引起的，但进一步分析显示，“地震事件是冰川崩塌和泥石流，对下游造成了后续灾难性影响”，“并没有发生地震”。 美国地质勘探局指出，当地时间周三上午 8 点 37 分，在尼泊尔和中国边境附近发生的冰川崩塌已被记录为里氏 5.2 级地震。 加拿大卡尔加里大学地貌学家 Daniel Shugar 副教授表示，初步卫星分析显示，一块 0.2 平方公里的冰块“垂直塌陷约 1.2 公里”。 “我从 Planet Labs 的卫星图像中看到，冰川下部在约 5,200 米处断裂，坠落到下方约 1,200 米的谷底，”他说道。 他在 Bluesky 上写道，这“很可能足以将大量潜力转化为动能（热能），从而融化冰”。 他说，卫星图像似乎还显示，灾难发生前 24 小时内大量积雪已经融化。 “山谷中的一些冰川昨天被雪覆盖，今天大部分都是裸露的冰。所以换句话说（我还没有看到任何气象站数据），天气可能很温暖。” 墨尔本莫纳什大学冰川学家安德鲁·麦金托什教授表示，目前尚不清楚此次崩塌是与冰川无关，还是“包括部分冰川在内的整个山坡崩塌”。 “当这种规模的冰川崩塌时，会产生大量的水，然后会发生一系列级联事件……水和沉积物结合在一起，体积增大，形成洪水。” 一个国际冰川研究小组表示，虽然冰川崩塌“肯定与此有关”，但“不太可能是唯一原因”。 “这种大型冰川崩塌确实令人震惊，”麦金托什说。 “作为一名冰川学家，很难不对这些似乎与我们之前观察到的不同的事件感到震惊。” 然而，他说“这些记录太少了，我们没有......

reflection.en: The devastating flash floods in the Nepal-Tibet border region, leaving scores dead and over a thousand missing, remind us of the profound grief and pain that can strike without warning. In moments of such widespread tragedy, our hearts ache for those who have lost loved ones and those still searching. Yahweh's promise in Revelation 21:4 offers a future hope...
reflection.zh: 尼泊尔-西藏边境地区毁灭性的山洪暴发，造成数十人死亡、一千多人失踪，提醒我们突如其来的深切悲痛和痛苦。在如此广泛的悲剧中，我们的心为那些失去亲人的人和仍在寻找的人而痛。雅伟在启示录21:4中的应许，为我们提供了一个未来的盼望，那时祂将擦去所有的眼泪，不再有死亡、悲哀、哭号和疼痛。

verse.textEn: He will wipe every tear from their eyes. There will be no more death or mourning or crying or pain.
verse.textZh: 神要擦去他们一切的眼泪；不再有死亡，也不再有悲哀、哭号、疼痛。

title.en: How the deadly Nepal and Tibet flash flood unfolded – a visual guide
title.zh: 尼泊尔和西藏致命山洪暴发始末——视觉指南

summary.en: A massive glacial collapse triggered catastrophic flash floods in the border region of Nepal and Tibet, resulting in at least 165 deaths and over 1,000 missing, including many tourists. The US Geological Survey confirmed the event.
summary.zh: 一场大规模的冰川崩塌引发了尼泊尔和西藏边境地区的灾难性山洪暴发，已造成至少165人死亡，超过1000人失踪，其中包括许多游客。美国地质调查局证实了这一事件。

body.en: US Geological Survey says massive glacial collapse caused catastrophic flash floods in the Himalayan border region of Nepal ⁠and Tibet Follow latest updates live Tell us: have you been affected by the flash floods? The massive glacial collapse that caused catastrophic flash floods in the Himalayan border region of Nepal ⁠and Tibet has killed at least 165 people, though the number of dead is set to rise, with local officials saying more than 1,000 were missing. Officials said 826 people were missing in Nepal, among them 579 tourists from two dozen countries, including India, the US, Australia, Britain and Canada. Chinese ‌state media said 558 people were missing ​in Tibet’s Gyirong ⁠county. It was not immediately clear if the missing counts were separate or some people been counted twice. Continue reading...
body.zh: 美国地质调查局表示，大规模的冰川崩塌在尼泊尔和西藏的喜马拉雅边境地区造成了灾难性的山洪 关注最新动态 告诉我们：您受到山洪的影响吗？大规模冰川崩塌在尼泊尔和西藏的喜马拉雅边境地区引发了灾难性山洪，已造成至少 165 人死亡，不过死亡人数还会上升，当地官员称有 1000 多人失踪。官员称，尼泊尔共有826人失踪，其中579名游客来自印度、美国、澳大利亚、英国和加拿大等二十几个国家。中国官方媒体称西藏吉隆县有 558 人失踪。目前尚不清楚缺失的计数是否是单独的，或者某些人被计数了两次。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The news of catastrophic flash floods in Nepal and Tibet, caused by a massive glacial collapse, brings to mind the deep groaning of creation itself. Romans 8:22 speaks of all creation groaning in the pains of childbirth, awaiting redemption. This event is a stark reminder of the fragility of our world and the profound disruptions it can experience.
reflection.zh: 尼泊尔和西藏因冰川崩塌引发灾难性山洪暴发的新闻，令人联想到受造之物自身的深沉叹息。罗马书8:22提到，万物一同叹息，劳苦直到如今。这一事件严峻地提醒我们世界的脆弱性，以及它可能经历的深刻动荡。

verse.textEn: We know that the whole creation has been groaning as in the pains of childbirth right up to the present time.
verse.textZh: 我们知道，一切受造之物一同叹息、劳苦，直到如今。

title.en: Australian tour group among 1,300 missing people in Nepal-Tibet floods
title.zh: 尼泊尔洪水和山体滑坡造成数百人失踪，其中包括澳大利亚人

summary.en: Aid workers have described scenes of complete destruction, with entire settlements "wiped out".
summary.zh: 救援人员描述了彻底毁灭的景象，整个定居点“被夷为平地”。

body.en:
Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has confirmed 34 Australians are missing after a massive flood and landslide disaster on the Nepal-Tibet border killed at least 165 people on Wednesday, with hundreds more unaccounted for.

Another 823 people, including 579 Nepali and foreign tourists, remained out of contact in Nepal, according to the country's disaster agency.

Across the border, Chinese state media said the "mudslide disaster" at the Gyirong Port in Tibet claimed three lives while 558 people, including 260 foreigners, were still missing.

"At this point, there are 34 Australians who are missing," Albanese told a press conference on Thursday morning. "People would have seen some of the footage, which is a truly horrific event."

Albanese said it was difficult to obtain information from Nepali authorities and appealed to anyone with information to come forward.

"At this point, Nepal is a developing country. It doesn't have the resources that an event like that would have in Australia, so information is difficult.

"Our thoughts are with all those who will be concerned about their loved ones today."

Defence minister Penny Wong echoed the Prime Minister's statements, noting that the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT) was working "urgently" to ascertain the welfare and location of the missing Australians.

"We are currently deploying further DFAT personnel, including crisis response experts to the region to ensure that we do provide the support needed to these posts, particularly our post in Nepal," Wong in a press conference on Thursday.

"At this stage, access and information are very limited given the scale of disaster. We will do our best, to ascertain whatever information we can."

A US-based tour company Himalayan Glacier Adventures told ABC News that 15 Australians, part of a group of 47 people, were on a hiking tour in the Lantang Valley at the time of the landslides.

The group of Australians was comprised of nine men and six women. Two of those Australians were reportedly boys aged 11 and 14, and a woman aged 64.

Tilak Pokharel, president of the Australian Nepalese Multicultural Centre, said there were "a lot" of people in Melbourne waiting anxiously to hear from loved ones.

"There are a lot of people affected by the flood. There are many people from that area living in Melbourne," Pokharel said.

"But several of them lost their property. I was just talking to someone who is from that area and they lost their houses, they lost their property and they have nothing left at the moment.

"I was talking to someone who was saying people went to see the flooding and they lost their life."

reflection.en: The news of hundreds missing and entire settlements "wiped out" by floods and landslides in Nepal brings immense sorrow. In moments of such widespread devastation and loss of life, the brevity of "Jesus wept" reminds us that grief is a natural and holy response. Yahweh, in Christ, shares in our human pain, offering a compassionate presence when words fail.

title.en: China advises its citizens to leave Taiwan ally Eswatini over 'security risks'
title.zh: 中国建议其公民因‘安全风险’离开台湾邦交国斯威士兰

summary.en: Eswatini is one of 12 countries, and the only one in Africa, that has diplomatic relations with Taiwan.
summary.zh: 斯威士兰是全球12个与台湾保持外交关系的国家之一，也是非洲唯一一个。

body.en:
China's foreign ministry has told its citizens to leave the southern African kingdom of Eswatini over "security risks".

The ministry cited "rampant cyber fraud and criminal activities associated with gambling" as among its security concerns, but did not give details.

It suggested its citizens relocate as soon as possible to "relatively safer" countries such as neighbouring South Africa.

Eswatini is one of 12 countries, and the only one in Africa, that has diplomatic relations with Taiwan, which China claims as part of its territory.

On Tuesday, the privately owned Times of Eswatini news site reported that 40 Chinese nationals have been in detention since last month , external after being arrested while trying to leave the country.

They were first arrested - along with dozens of other foreign nationals - in March during raids on alleged illegal online gambling centres in the main city, Mbabane, and surrounding areas, the news site reported.

The group's lawyers had written to the attorney general and home affairs ministry, stating that they had pleaded guilty to immigration-related offences and had paid fines imposed by the courts, the news site reported.

The 40 were then released on the orders of the High Court, and their re-arrest was unlawful, the lawyers were quoted as saying.

In its advisory to its citizens, China says those who insist on travelling to or staying in the country will face "extremely high security risks, and the timeliness of assistance may be affected".

China has for years pressured countries to end diplomatic relations with Taiwan.

In April, Taiwan accused Beijing of trying to derail its President Lai Ching-te's travel to Eswatini by pressuring nearby countries to revoke overflight permits.

The trip, originally planned for 22-26 April to mark the 40th anniversary of Eswatini's King Mswati III's accession, was cancelled following the development.

Lai eventually travelled to Eswatini in May, without saying how he reached the country. None of the governments had announced the trip beforehand.

Following the visit, Beijing's foreign ministry said that Lai had become "an international laughing stock".

Earlier this year, China scrapped tariffs for all African countries, except Eswatini.
body.zh: 由于“安全风险”，中国外交部已要求其公民离开南部非洲斯威士兰王国。 该部将“猖獗的网络欺诈和与赌博相关的犯罪活动”列为其安全担忧之一，但没有提供细节。 它建议其公民尽快搬迁到邻国南非等“相对安全”的国家。 斯威士兰是 12 个国家之一，也是非洲唯一一个与台湾建交的国家，中国声称台湾是其领土的一部分。 周二，私营新闻网站《斯威士兰时报》报道称，自上个月以来，已有 40 名中国公民在试图离开该国时被捕，并在境外被拘留。 据新闻网站报道，他们与其他数十名外国人一起于 3 月份在对主要城市姆巴巴内及周边地区涉嫌非法在线赌博中心的突袭中首次被捕。 据新闻网站报道，该组织的律师已写信给总检察长和内政部，表示他们已承认与移民有关的罪行，并已支付法院判处的罚款。 律师称，这 40 人随后根据高等法院的命令被释放，再次逮捕他们是非法的。 中国在给公民的建议中表示，那些坚持前往或留在中国的人将面临“极高的安全风险，援助的及时性可能受到影响”。 多年来，中国一直向各国施压，要求它们终止与台湾的外交关系。 今年四月，台湾指责北京试图向周边国家施压，要求吊销飞越许可，从而破坏台湾总统赖清德前往斯威士兰的行程。 这次旅行原计划于4月22日至26日举行，以纪念斯威士兰国王姆斯瓦蒂三世登基40周年，但因事态发展而被取消。 赖最终于五月前往斯威士兰，但没有透露他是如何到达该国的。没有任何一个政府事先宣布这次访问。 访问结束后，北京外交部表示赖已成为“国际笑柄”。 今年早些时候，中国取消了对除斯威士兰以外的所有非洲国家的关税。

reflection.en: The news of China advising its citizens to leave Eswatini due to 'rampant cyber fraud and criminal activities associated with gambling' highlights the importance of discerning danger. Proverbs 27:12 reminds us that the prudent see danger and take refuge. In a world with complex security risks, wisdom calls for recognizing threats and taking necessary steps...
reflection.zh: 中国建议其公民因“猖獗的网络诈骗和与赌博相关的犯罪活动”离开斯威士兰的消息，凸显了辨别危险的重要性。箴言27:12提醒我们，通达人见祸藏躲。在一个充满复杂安全风险的世界里，智慧要求我们识别威胁并采取必要措施保护自己和他人。

verse.textEn: The prudent see danger and take refuge, but the simple keep going and pay the penalty.
verse.textZh: 通达人见祸藏躲；愚蒙人前往受害。

title.en: Deadly flash flood wipes away villages in Nepal, Tibet
title.zh: 尼泊尔和西藏突发致命洪灾，多个村庄被冲毁

summary.en: Dozens of people have died and hundreds are missing after flash floods swept through remote valleys in Nepal and Tibet. Rescue efforts have been hampered by high water levels, preventing helicopters from landing, while authorities work to relocate families from high-risk areas. At least 157 bodies have been recovered...
summary.zh: 尼泊尔和西藏的偏远山谷遭遇突发洪灾，造成数十人死亡，数百人失踪。由于水位过高，救援直升机无法降落，救援工作严重受阻。目前当局正努力将高风险地区的家庭转移，警方已找回157具遗体，失踪人员中还包括341名外国游客。

body.en:
Dozens have died and hundreds were reported missing, including 341 foreign tourists. Rescue helicopters have been unable to land in affected areas due to high floodwaters.

Dozens of people were confirmed dead and hundreds more are missing after a flash flood swept through remote valleys in Nepal and Tibet on Wednesday.

Nepali police said that authorities have recovered 157 bodies. Officers were "working to move families in flood-risk areas... to safer locations," police said.

"The pain and loss you have suffered is not small. But I want to assure you that you are not alone in this difficult time -- the state is with you with all its means and resources," Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah said in a statement posted to social media. "Please be patient. The government takes full responsibility for your rescue, treatment, food and shelter. In times of such a disaster, we all need to stand together."

In China, authorities said at least three have died, with 265 still missing, China's state broadcaster CCTV ‌said.

The floodwaters washed away villages, damaged bridges and destroyed electrical infrastructure on both sides of the Nepal-China border.

"There is devastation everywhere we look," ‌Tula ​Bahadur BK, a health worker in Rasuwa district, told Reuters.

"The settlements next to the river have been completely swept away. Five of my own relatives are missing."

At the same time, Chinese authorities also reported that a mudslide caused "major casualties" on the other side of the border in Tibet.

Nepal's Tourism Ministry said 403 travelers were reported missing for several hours after the floods struck. 

In China, the Xinhua state news agency reported Thursday that the number of missing people had increased to 558. State broadcaster CCTV reported that 260 of the missing people were foreigners.

Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said Thursday that 34 Australians were missing following the flash flooding. 

"Our thoughts are with all those who will be concerned about their loved ones today," Albanese said.

A Nepali police spokesperson told Germany's DPA news agency that dozens of personnel were also missing.

"So far, we only have confirmation of 26 police personnel who remain missing in the flood," they said.

"We also have missing information of government revenue officials, hydropower workers among others. But we are still collecting the data."

Nepal's Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal said an earthquake triggered an avalanche in the Himalayas that then triggered flash floods in the valleys below.

Chinese state news agency Xinhua said a mudslide on the Nepali side of the mountains spread to Gyirong County in Tibet.

title.en: China: Dissident artist jailed for satirical Mao sculptures
title.zh: 中国：持不同政见艺术家因讽刺毛泽东雕塑而入狱

summary.en: Sculptor Gao Zhen was charged under China's "Law on the Protection ⁠of Heroes ​and Martyrs." His supporters have called for his immediate release.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自中国栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Sculptor Gao Zhen was charged under China's "Law on the Protection ⁠of Heroes ​and Martyrs." His supporters have called for his immediate release.

A court in China has reportedly sentenced a dissident artist to three years in jail for sculptures which satirized former Chinese revolutionary leader Mao Zedong .

Sculptor Gao Zhen, 70, became famous in the 2000s for addressing sensitive topics in China such as the 1966-1976 Cultural Revolution or the 1989 Tiananmen Square massacre through artworks he produced with his younger brother Gao Qiang.

Zhen, who is based in New York , was arrested during a visit to Beijing in August 2024. He was tried this year ⁠in a ⁠one-day behind-closed-doors trial and found guilty of "infringing upon the reputation of heroes."

"We feel outraged," Gao's wife Zhao Yaliang told the Reuters news agency. "Ever since I learned of the ​verdict, I haven't been able to recover from it. It's devastating."

Zhao also said she and her son, who is a US citizen, had been barred from leaving China since Zhen's detention two years ago.

Zhen was charged under China's "Law on the Protection ⁠of Heroes ​and Martyrs," legislation which came into effect in 2018 and was strengthened in ​2021.

The artworks found to have broken the law, however, date to 2005 and 2009, according to Shane Yi, a researcher at Chinese Human Rights Defenders who has been advocating for Gao's case.

"The court has now sentenced him to three years ... for artwork he made as far back as 2005, some 16 years before the law he was charged under even existed," Yi told Reuters, calling the punishment "a very clear case of a violation of a person's freedom of expression."

The artworks in question are reported to be "Mao's Guilt," a 2009 bronze statue of the former leader kneeling remorsefully, and the "Miss Mao" series of caricatures which depict Mao with breasts and a Pinocchio-like nose.

"No artist should face criminal punishment for creating work that challenges official narratives or encourages critical reflection on history," Amnesty's China Director Sarah Brooks told the Associated Press.

"The lengthy pre-trial detention and, ultimately, decision to convict Gao Zhen and sentence him to the maximum three-year prison term under this offense illustrate the authorities' determination to deter others from engaging in independent artistic expression."

Researcher Yi said: "The only outcome that respects Gao Zhen's rights is his immediate, unconditional release."

body.zh: 雕塑家高震被指控违反中国《英雄烈士保护法》。他的支持者呼吁立即释放他。 据报道，中国一家法院因讽刺前中国革命领袖毛泽东的雕塑而判处一名异见艺术家三年监禁。 70 岁的雕塑家高震在 2000 年代因与弟弟高强创作的作品探讨中国的敏感话题而闻名，例如 1966-1976 年的文化大革命或 1989 年的天安门广场大屠杀。 甄现居住在纽约，于 2024 年 8 月访问北京期间被捕。今年，他在为期一天的闭门审判中接受审判，并被判犯有“侵犯英雄声誉”罪。 “我们感到愤怒，”高的妻子赵亚良告诉路透社。 “自从我得知判决后，我一直无法从中恢复过来。这是毁灭性的。” 赵还表示，自从两年前甄被拘留以来，她和她的美国公民儿子就被禁止离开中国。 甄根据中国《英雄烈士保护法》受到指控，该法于 2018 年生效，并于 2021 年加强。 然而，据一直为高案辩护的中国人权卫士研究员谢恩·易 (Shane Yi) 表示，被发现违法的艺术品可追溯到 2005 年和 2009 年。 易告诉路透社，“法院现在判处他三年有期徒刑……因为他早在 2005 年就创作了艺术品，比他被指控的法律还早大约 16 年。”他称这一处罚是“一个非常明显的侵犯个人言论自由的案件”。 据报道，这些艺术品是2009年创作的前领导人悔恨跪下的铜像“毛泽东的罪孽”，以及描绘毛泽东胸部和匹诺曹鼻子的“毛小姐”系列漫画。 国际特赦组织中国部主任萨拉·布鲁克斯 (Sarah Brooks) 告诉美联社：“任何艺术家都不应因创作挑战官方叙述或鼓励对历史进行批判性反思的作品而面临刑事处罚。” “长时间的审前拘留，以及最终决定对高震定罪并判处他最高三年徒刑，表明当局决心阻止其他人从事独立的艺术表达。” 易研究员说：“尊重高震权利的唯一结果就是立即无条件释放他。” 如果您信赖我们团队的可信报道，请花点时间选择我们作为您在 Google 上的首选来源，这样您始终会首先看到我们经过验证的新闻。

reflection.en: This story draws attention to justice, dignity, and accountability. Micah 6:8 reminds us to meet sharp headlines with justice tempered by mercy, asking how faithful people can respond with wisdom instead of noise.

title.en: 'Can't abstain from this debate': Pacific nations the next frontier in deep-sea mining
title.zh: “无法回避的辩论”：太平洋国家成为深海采矿的下一个前沿

summary.en: A new report warns that commercial deep-sea mining in the Pacific could begin as early as 2027, driven by increasing rivalry between the United States and China for critical minerals. Pacific nations are reportedly split between the promise of economic benefits and the risk of irreversible damage to the environment...
summary.zh: 一份新报告警告称，由于美国和中国之间对关键矿产的竞争日益加剧，太平洋地区的商业深海采矿可能最早在2027年开始。据报道，太平洋国家在经济利益的承诺与对环境和当地生计造成不可逆转损害的风险之间存在分歧。

body.en:
Commercial deep-sea mining in the Pacific could begin in months without policy guardrails due to increasing rivalry between the United States and China over critical minerals, a new report warns.

Analysis by the Lowy Institute has found mining could start as early as 2027, with the floor of the Pacific Ocean holding vast quantities of prized resources.

The contest between the world's two biggest economies is being driven by demand created by batteries, weapons systems, and power grids.

The region's nations are split between the promise of economic spoils and the risk of irreversible damage to the ecosystem, fisheries, food security, livelihoods and culture, according to the research.

It argues the absence of an international governance framework for commercial deep-sea mining leaves Pacific states negotiating without internationally agreed protections.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

This also leaves them dependent on individual agreements drafted by companies seeking to mine their ocean floor.

"For the Pacific Island nations caught in the middle of this great power battle for critical mineral supremacy, the economic proposition is difficult to refuse," the Lowy Institute's Connor Graham writes.

"The problem is not that Pacific nations disagree, it is that they are being forced to negotiate individually against parties with vastly more resources, information, and legal capacity, and that the international framework designed to protect them has stalled."

Graham said while Australia was yet to take a clear position on deep-sea mining in the Pacific, it has the standing, relationships, and institutional presence to make an impact.

This includes its membership in the Pacific Islands Forum and as a long-standing ally of the US.

"A commitment to standards that have not been written as a condition for activity that is about to begin is less of a policy, and more of an abstention," he said.

Countries including Australia have started to enter into deals for critical minerals, which are crucial for a number for emerging technologies.

The federal government has announced a $1.2 billion critical minerals strategic reserve to secure the supply of key minerals deemed crucial for Australia's economy and national security.

For the latest from SBS News, download our app and subscribe to our newsletter .
body.zh: 一份新报告警告称，由于美国和中国在关键矿产方面的竞争日益激烈，太平洋地区的商业深海采矿可能会在没有政策保护的情况下在几个月内开始。 洛伊研究所的分析发现，采矿最早可能在 2027 年开始，太平洋海底蕴藏着大量珍贵资源。 全球最大的两个经济体之间的竞争是由电池、武器系统和电网产生的需求驱动的。 研究表明，该地区各国在经济收益的承诺和生态系统、渔业、粮食安全、生计和文化遭受不可逆转损害的风险之间存在分歧。 它认为，商业深海采矿国际治理框架的缺乏导致太平洋国家在没有国际商定保护的情况下进行谈判。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 这也使得它们依赖于寻求海底采矿的公司起草的单独协议。 洛伊研究所的康纳·格雷厄姆写道：“对于陷入这场争夺关键矿产霸权的大国战争的太平洋岛国来说，这个经济提议很难拒绝。” “问题不在于太平洋国家不同意，而在于它们被迫与拥有更多资源、信息和法律能力的各方进行单独谈判，而旨在保护它们的国际框架已经陷入停滞。” 格雷厄姆表示，虽然澳大利亚尚未对太平洋深海采矿采取明确立场，但它拥有产生影响的地位、关系和机构存在。 这包括它是太平洋岛屿论坛的成员以及美国的长期盟友。 他说：“对尚未作为即将开始的活动条件的标准的承诺与其说是一项政策，不如说是一种弃权。” 包括澳大利亚在内的国家已开始签订关键矿物交易，这对许多新兴技术至关重要。 联邦政府宣布设立 12 亿美元的关键矿产战略储备，以确保对澳大利亚经济和国家安全至关重要的关键矿产的供应。 如需了解 SBS 新闻的最新动态，请下载我们的应用程序并订阅我们的时事通讯。

reflection.en: The prospect of deep-sea mining in the Pacific presents a stark choice for island nations, balancing potential economic gains against the risk of irreversible ecological damage. As the report warns of mining commencing without adequate policy guardrails, the words of 1 Corinthians 10:23 remind us that while many actions may be permissible, not all are truly...
reflection.zh: 太平洋深海采矿的前景给岛屿国家带来了严峻的选择，需要在潜在的经济收益与不可逆转的生态破坏风险之间取得平衡。正如报告警告，在缺乏充分政策保障的情况下，采矿可能即将开始，哥林多前书10:23提醒我们，虽然许多事情是合法的，但并非所有事情都有益处或能造就人。这种情况呼唤智慧，以辨别什么能真正造就社区并保护雅伟的创造，而不是仅仅追求权宜之计。
